articleTitle: Ultrawideband Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for Non-Contact Biomedical Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This study introduces a compact ultrawideband (UWB) antipodal Vivaldi antenna designed for non-contact biomedical sensing applications. The antenna features a tapered slot structure optimized for enhanced bandwidth and gain, providing reliable impedance matching across an extensive frequency range from 3.6 GHz to 11.3 GHz. Constructed on a textile substrate with a dielectric constant of 1.6 and a loss tangent of 0.025, the design employs a 1 Oz (0.035 mm) copper patch. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 9.85 dBi, meeting the high-performance demands for precise, non-invasive bio-sensing. The compact design and broad fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 103.3% make it highly suitable for biomedical diagnostics, enabling effective biomedical sensing applications.

articleTitle: Design of mm Wave Sensor for the Prognosis of Burn Wounds Severity Using Arm Tissue Phantom
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Recent developments in wearable and flexible electronics coupled with Internet of Things have created new developments in smart healthcare yet chronic wound monitoring still receives little attention from researchers. Accurate and early diagnoses of chronic skin wounds yield numerous benefits for the patient. mmWave devices monitor skin wounds through variations in S-parameters with our research focusing on S11. Healthy skin and burnt tissues have different dielectric properties. The variations of these dielectric properties cause changes in S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> which can be seen on an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> plot as a frequency shift. Tissue Mimicking Material (TMM), also known as Tissue Phantoms, have been created to replicate the dielectric properties of skin, fat, muscle, and bone tissue. These phantoms were stacked on top of each other to create an arm tissue phantom. Numerous arm tissue phantoms were created, and they included: healthy tissue (no burns), first-degree burn, second-degree burn, and third-degree burn. This was done by burning the skin tissue phantoms to various degrees. After these arm tissue phantoms were synthesized and burned, the values of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> were measured and recorded from two different patch antennas that were resonant at 18 GHz. Results of these S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> plots show that there is a frequency shift between the health, first-, second-and third-degree burn tissue phantom.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Al2O3 for Millimeter Wave Metalens
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this letter, we present a millimeter wave (mmWave) metalens with a gradient refractive index (GRIN) profile. Gradient metamaterials with exquisite structures are designed and manufactured by 3D-printed Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> to realize the corresponding gradient refractive index in the frequency range of 90 GHz to 110 GHz. Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>'s properties of low loss and stable refractive index in the mmWave range will contribute to the achromatic focusing and high transmittance, which is of significant importance in mmWave/THz imaging. Measured electric field distributions demonstrate that achromatic focusing could be achieved with a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.3. The derived full width at half maximum (FWHM) is about 1.5λ. This work proves that ceramic 3D printing technology holds strong potential for wide-ranging applications within the mmWave/THz field.

articleTitle: “The Crossed Loop Antenna”
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A crossed loop / half loop antenna is described providing dual circular polarization and hemispherical radiation patterns for space applications. Usefully isotropic radiation is provided if the ground plane is omitted. Good radiation efficiency is provided at diminutive electrically small size. Capacitor loading allows tuning over at 10:1 frequency range and wide adjustment in size. Inductive coupling loops are used to realize a novel hybrid power divider in situ. Applications include aviation, satellite, GPS and terrestrial communications. Simple wire construction is shown.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Antenna Leveraging Piezoelectric Resonance in Stacked Layers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Antenna miniaturization is applicable to many mobile communications applications where size, and weight, and power consumption are important design parameters. Recently there has been interest in electrically small antennae that leverage mechanical resonance and the piezoelectric effect to achieve several orders of magnitude performance improvements over metallic counterparts. This paper proposes a novel piezoelectric antenna structure utilizing stacked alternating polarization layers capable of scaling to larger electrical sizes while maintaining a usable impedance. The proposed structure was evaluated using a full wave piezoelectric finite element model at a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ka=7\times 10^{-3}$</tex> achieving a real impedance of 52.5 ohms and a theoretical radiation efficiency of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.08\times 10^{-5}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Performance of Screen-Printed Wearable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: As the wearable industry continues to grow, body centric wearable systems are gaining interest for healthcare and military applications. Despite this growth, integrating wireless communication into flexible textile substrates remains to be an ongoing challenge. In this study, the performance of various screen-printed wearable patch antennas on different textiles is investigated. The textiles considered are 100% Cotton Twill, 65/35% Polyester-Cotton, 82/18% Spandex-Nylon and 100% Spandex. To ensure consistency, the ACI Silver Conductor Ink (FS0142) is used for all screen-printed antennas. The investigated performance parameters are the return loss, gain and radiation pattern. Further, the durability of each antenna is tested by a wash study, stretch and heat test.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Efficient Metasurface Absorber for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this contribution, a single-layer metasurface absorber is proposed for collecting the ambient radio frequency energy at 2.45 GHz. A design methodology is proposed to optimize the finite array performance. An absorber of 4×5 cells is designed and simulated to demonstrate that this methodology enables an improvement of the capturing efficiency from 65% to 90%. The proposed finite array is fabricated and its capturing efficiency is measured in order to be compared to a simulation.

articleTitle: Measurement of Propagation Impact by Low-E Glass From Outdoor Base Stations to Indoor of a House in 800 MHz to 3.7 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: It is becoming increasingly common for houses to be constructed with high levels of insulation, and the use of Low-E glass is also becoming more prevalent. However, the utilization of Low-E glass has the unintended consequence of also blocking radio waves in addition to heat. This paper presents the results of an investigation into the propagation of radio waves in the 5G mobile communication band, from 800 MHz to 3.7 GHz, from an outdoor base station to an indoor location within a house. The study compares the performance of Low-E glass in the presence and absence of the radio waves comparing to the individual materials of the glass.

articleTitle: Using Gallium-Based Liquid Metal to Create Beam Switchable Bull's Eye Antennas
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents two designs for beam switchable Bulls Eye antennas. The first beam switchable antenna was generated by dividing a Bull's Eye antenna into two symmetrical halves. We can then reconfigure the beam direction by effectively switching each half on and off. We refer to this design, throughout the paper, as a beam switchable Bull's Eye antenna. The second design effectively involves switching between two different antenna types having different main beam directions, namely: a Bull's Eye and a Yagi-Uda. We refer to this design, throughout the paper, as a two-mode antenna. In order to enable us to switch between the two different types of antennas, we nest the geometrical features of the Yagi-Uda antenna inside those of the Bull's Eye antenna. The beam switchable Bull's Eye antenna operates at a frequency of 10 GHz and the two-mode antenna operates at a frequency of 15 GHz. Both antennas incorporate a series of fluidic channels. In practical prototypes of the antennas, they would be reconfigured by filling and emptying different combinations of channels with Gallium-based liquid metal. The main beam of the beam switchable Bull's Eye antenna can scan between ±14°. At 10 GHz, simulated realized gain was 12.1 dBi, with a sidelobe level (SSL) of -9.3 dB. The simulated main beam of the two-mode antenna can be switched from 1° (for the Bull's Eye mode) to 74° (for the Yagi-Uda mode). The simulated realised gain was 13 dB and 16.2 dB for the for Yagi-Uda and Bull's Eye mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Flexible and Stretchable Antenna Using Corrugated Copper-Clad Polyimide and Beyolex Film
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Copper-clad polyimide film (CCPF) is combined with Beyolex transparent film to realize a lightweight flexible, stretchable, and foldable antenna. The antenna is designed for 1.20 GHz using a corrugated patch and the ground plane using CCPFs. The corrugations on both sides of the antenna facilitate complete bending in both concave and convex directions. The antenna is fabricated and tested for various bending and stretching scenarios. The antenna has an impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 2.0% and gain of 7.8 dBi at 1.20 GHz under normal conditions. The antenna is tested by conforming it to cylinders with radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{c}$</tex> = 200, 160, 100, 80, 40, and 20 mm. The antenna gain values are slightly reduced from 7.8 dBi to 6.2 dBi while reducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{c}$</tex> from 200 mm to 40 mm. The antenna resonant frequency shifts from 1.20 GHz to 1.21 GHz when applying a strain of 6.3% to 18.8%.

articleTitle: Operational Characteristics of a Plasma Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Through a combination of S-Parameter measurements, radiation patterns, and surface wave excitation measurements, we present a comprehensive picture of the operational characteristics of a laboratory prototype plasma antenna. It is shown that the current is driven along the plasma column by surface waves, which lead to a broad band absorption of input signal power and directly is reflected in the measurements of the transmitted radiation pattern. The plasma antenna is observed to operate over a much broader range of frequency compared to a metal antenna of similar dimensions. These experimental results should provide a much more coherent picture of how this device operates.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Implantable Multiband Circular Polarized Antenna with Meandered Structure for Wireless Power and Data Transfer in Neuromodulation Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, bio-compatible and miniaturized multi-band antenna with circular polarization (CP) behavior is presented for wireless power transfer at 2.4 GHz and wireless data transmission at 5.8 GHz Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) bands. Initially, an antenna based on H-shaped resonator is developed and then meander-line structure is employed and optimized for size reduction and impedance matching. The proposed multi-band antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0.16}\lambda_{o}\times 0{.16\lambda_{o}}$</tex> dimension for 2.4 GHz operating frequency which depicts 6.2% impedance bandwidth and 18.96% AR bandwidth. The specific absorption rate (SAR) of the proposed antenna is assessed and it complies with the health safety limit (SAR < 1.6 W/kg).

articleTitle: H-Plane Coupled Yagi-Uda mm-Wave ESPAR Array
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A Yagi-Uda electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna array is proposed for mm-Wave beamsteering applications. The 3-element array is designed using YagiUda antenna elements, each with a dipole element and a ground plane reflector, coupled in the H-plane. The design operates from 27.5 GHz − 30 GHz with 9% usable fractional bandwidth. By terminating the parasitic element feed lines with tunable reactive loads, the array is capable of beam steering to +/- 30° in simulation with 6 dBi gain.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray Using Vanadium Dioxide for 5G mmWave Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) reconfigurable reflectarray was designed and simulated for operation between 28–32 GHz. VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is an insulator-metal-transition phase-change material that exhibits a sharp, reversible conductivity change at 68 °C. The design is dual-polarized to support LP, dual-LP, or dual-CP applications. The simulated reflection loss is less than 1 dB over the entire band. The phase difference is 180 ± 20° between 28–33 GHz. The simulated realized gain of the finite array peaks at 22.9 dBi, which corresponds to an aperture efficiency of 29%. The 3-dB Gain bandwidth covers 27.7-33.2 GHz, which is an 18% bandwidth. Ongoing fabrication and measurement results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis of Sparse Linear Arrays with Mutual Coupling Using Vectorial Matrix Pencil Method
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A challenging research question is how to achieve a desired pattern of an antenna array with the least number of antenna elements while including mutual coupling. The matrix pencil method (MPM) simplifies the derivation by assuming that the elements are isotropic and that there is no mutual coupling. However, in practical engineering, the desired pattern is scalar while the element patterns are vectorial and different due to the presence of mutual coupling, rendering traditional MPM less applicable. Here, a vectorial MPM (VMPM) is presented that takes mutual coupling effects into account. First, a Hankel sampling matrix is constructed from the desired radiation pattern, and singular value decomposition (SVD) is performed to obtain the minimum number of elements. Next, the sampling matrix is used to construct the matrix pencil to determine the positions of the elements. Furthermore, intelligent optimization algorithms are introduced to obtain the element excitations considering mutual coupling effects. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by a numerical case.

articleTitle: A 4×4 L-Band Dual-Polarized Array with Digital Transmit/Receive Beamforming Using RFSoC
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A 4×4 L-band dual-polarized differential-fed patch antenna array with full digital beamforming using radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) is presented. Each of the 16 dual-polarized antenna units has good impedance matching from 1.2 to 1.3 GHz with an isolation larger than 30 dB. The array performance is first validated using analog beamforming at boresight using a 1:16 power divider. The measured realized gain is more than 16.8 dBi within the 1.2 to 1.3 GHz bandwidth. Subsequently, the array is combined with the ZCU216 RFSoC and full digital beamforming for both transmit and receive is demonstrated with independent beamforming capability for each polarization.

articleTitle: The All Polarization Helix Antenna: The Sine Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: An all-polarization equivalent of the Axial Mode Helix Antenna (AMHA) is described. Projections of the helix on a cylindrical envelope define one or more sine radiating elements. A single beam axially directive radiation is provided. All polarizations can be synthesized: linear, circular, and dual polarizations. Directivity for length can exceed that of the Axial Mode Helix Antenna and the Yagi-Uda Antenna. 50-ohm coaxial feed is provided. Construction by flexible printed circuit board wrap is shown.

articleTitle: Design and Development of K/Ka-Band Flat Panel Phased Array Antennas and Data Throughput Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This article presents the details of some of the latest flat-panel active electronically scanned phased arrays (AESA) that were designed and developed at the Antenna and Microwave Laboratory (AML), San Diego State University. The described research works were conducted in collaboration with Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC-PAC); United States Army Command, Control, Communication, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) Center; and National Aeronautics and Space Administration Glenn Research Center (NASA-GRC). The designed phased array antennas were characterized at the AML by measuring their beam scanning and over-the-Air (OTA) data throughput performances.

articleTitle: The Role of Photonic Devices in Advanced Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper we introduce novel radio-frequency-photonic (RF-photonic) components, such as advanced electro-optic modulators (EOMs) and high-power photodetectors (PDs), and their application to advanced phased array systems. In addition, by strongly leveraging the microelectronics manufacturing industry, chip-scale optical systems have been implemented using photonic integrated circuits (PICs), which enable a profound reduction in size, weight, and power (SWaP). Such advances are destined to have a significant impact on the development, application, and commercialization of next generation phased array systems, particularly for phased array transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) antennas that provide ultra-wideband operation with time-of-flight full beamspace processing, with near unlimited beam bandwidth products (BBP). Accordingly, this paper presents phased array systems that performs massive beamspace processing in such a way as to render a realtime image of the passive RF environment. On the active signal side, a similar phased array system has demonstrated simultaneous, broadband multi-beam, multi-band, and multi-data processing. These systems have achieved upwards of a BBP of over 10 THz.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Tunable Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A two-dimensional tunable Butler matrix is presented in this paper, where two 4×4 tunable Butler matrices are stacked in a vertical configuration to achieve a progressive phase difference in the horizontal direction. Four tunable couplers are applied to the 8 output ports of the stacked tunable Butler matrices and achieve progressive phase tuning in the vertical direction. By combining two dimensions of progressive phase, a two-dimensional radiation beam is formed and thus permits the beam to be continuously steered by controlling the bias voltage of varactors embedded in the tunable transmission line within the Butler matrix.

articleTitle: An AI-Powered RIS Technology for Hand Gesture Recognition in the Radiating Near Field
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper focuses on using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) for gesture recognition through AI with experimental data. Using a mono-static setup of a RIS, 4.9 – 5 GHz radio waves can be directly beamed at a hand, which reflects the incident wave depending on the hand gesture. The received reflection signal from the hand is processed and given to a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The CNN performs with a prediction accuracy of 97.65%. Through this it is shown that it is possible to use an AI-powered RIS to recognise simple hand gestures, thereby adding to hand gesture recognition methods, and expanding on integrated sensing and communication (ISAC).

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Dual Independently-Tunable Near-Field Focus Metasurface for Advanced Radar Bio-Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The demand for advanced, non-invasive blood glucose monitoring technologies has driven extensive research into radar sensing applications. This paper introduces a dual-band, dual independently-tunable near-field focus metasurface designed to enhance the performance of millimeter (mm)-wave radar-based bio-sensor. This metasurface enables dual focusing of absorbed power within human skin, achieved through a phase-synthesized analysis of the metasurface array, where each focal point is controlled by a distinct frequency band within the radar spectrum. The integration of the proposed metallic slot metasurface with commercially available Infineon radar TX/RX antennas results in a 14.7 dB and 12.4 dB increase in Poynting power density at two distinct points within a human skin phantom model, along with an increase in radar-received power by 11 dB and 12.7 dB at 58.5 GHz and 61.7 GHz, respectively, significantly enhancing the radar's bio-sensing capabilities.

articleTitle: High-Power Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray for Directed Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A high-power dual-polarized reconfigurable reflectar ray with all-metal antenna elements is presented for directed energy applications. The reflectaarry is comprised of 4-port antenna element that incorporates stacked 2-bit phase shifters for reconfiguration. Key to the design is the all-metal antenna, designed to endure intense radiation and harsh environmental conditions. Further, a Cassagrain sub-reflector is included to maximize the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of the high-power reflectarray system. Simulations demonstrated that the proposed unit cell design can achieve a full 0° - 360° phase shift. Additionally, it was observed that the antenna unit cell offers a gain of 5 dBi to 6.5 dBi at operating frequencies after reflection. A reflectarray prototype of 2m×2m, comprising the proposed 4-port unit cells will be constructed to steer the beam and serve as validation.

articleTitle: Characteristics Measurement of Wearable Embroidered Disc-Shaped Textile Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In the fast growing of wearable devices, textile-based antennas play a critical role in achieving reliable wireless and mobile communications. This paper deals with an experimental approach for measuring the radiation characteristics of a wearable embroidered disc-shaped textile array antenna which is designed based on microstrip technology and realized using cotton-fabric. The proposed array antenna utilizes cotton-fabric as the host substrate and copper wires embroidered manually to form a four-element disc-shaped array. Five square layers of cotton-fabric with the thickness of 0.2 mm each are used to construct the array antenna. The measured characteristics yield a wideband frequency response of 2.52 GHz from the frequency of 2.76 GHz to 5.28 GHz with the lowest reflection coefficient value of -29.92 dB at the frequency of 3.42 GHz. In addition, the measured radiation patterns demonstrate unidirectional types, which are similar to that of a typical microstrip patch array antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized and Multi-Axis Foldable Antenna Using Sequentially Arranged Conformal Patches
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A simple, lightweight, multi-axis bendable and foldable antenna based on flexible copper-clad polyimide (FCCPM) patches is presented. First, a single antenna is designed comprising a semi-elliptical shaped conformal patch operating at 1.25 GHz. The single antenna is used to design a four-element antenna by rotating each additional element sequentially. Dual polarization (DP) is achieved by exciting the conformal antenna pairs with equal magnitude and 180° phase difference. The DP antenna provides a 10 dB return loss bandwidth of 20%, isolation better than 20 dB, and gain of 7.6 dBi at 1.25 GHz. Antennas are analyzed for the flat case and conformed to cylinders in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions with radius of 200, 160, 150, 100, and 80 mm.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Metamaterial Antenna Design with Superstrate for B5G FR3 Bands Using Osprey Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this work, we present an antenna design for operation between 21 and 23 GHz in the FR3 band for B5G and 6G operation. The proposed antenna uses a metamaterial super-strate for gain and bandwidth enhancement. We optimize the geometrical parameters using a recently proposed evolutionary algorithm, namely the Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA), which imitates the behavior of osprey in nature. The OOA finds a design with wideband operation and gain enchantment. The proposed low-profile antenna yields a peak gain of about 8.9 dBi around 22 GHz. The antenna exhibits a frequency band with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11} < -10 d B$</tex> ranging from 19.21 to 23.38 GHz.

articleTitle: A Three-Axis, Dual-Feed, Shielded Loop Probe Incorporating a Re-Entrant Infinite Balun
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The realization of a 3-axis magnetic-field probe system comprising three orthogonal, co-located, shielded loops presents some difficulties; in particular, the preservation of balance and isolation. Lack of balance results in an undesirable electric field response as well as degradation of the intrinsic isolation. This has been shown to be because the common-mode (CM) electric field responses of the loops are significantly coupled, even when all three loops are perfectly orthogonal to one another. Exploiting two diametrically located feeds in each loop can more effectively enforce balance but then requires an internal balancing mechanism. Previous work has employed internal Guanella current baluns with magnetic cores and reasonably good performance was obtained. However, limitations in isolation were noticed and found to be due to the internal baluns. Here, an internal, re-entrant infinite balun realized with a triaxial cross section is exploited to obtain improved balance and isolation.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Multi-Wideband Antenna for Variable-Size Tablet Computers and Mobile Phones
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper discusses a miniaturized multi-wideband tablet antenna having a compact size of 20 × 9.6 × 1.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna is modeled on FR-4 substrate with thickness of 0.8 mm. The antenna covers LTE 700/2300/2500/3500, GPS 1575.42 MHz, GSM 850/1800/1900, UMTS 2100, Bluetooth 2.4 GHz and 5.2/5.8 GHz WLAN bands. The wideband operation is achieved by a novel inverted-F type structure which is capacitively coupled with two λ/4 microstrip resonators. Impedance matching at lower bands is further improved by a high-pass matching circuit integrated with the antenna feed. The proposed antenna has reasonable gain over all covered bands, low specific absorption rate (SAR) and high radiation efficiency from 80-90% over all LTE and WLAN bands.

articleTitle: High-Contrast Low-Loss Antennas with Improved Bandwidth and Wearability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: We recently presented a new class of antennas for into-body radiation with unprecedented performance, namely, High-Contrast Low-Loss Antennas (HCLAs). The HCLAs, however, were limited by their size and bandwidth capabilities. Into-body antennas should be conformal to the body for wearable applications. Additionally, lower frequencies should be targeted due to their larger penetration depths into the tissues. To overcome these challenges, we herewith propose to (a) reduce the height, and (b) improve the low frequency cutoff, without compromising antenna performance. Simulations and measurements verify that the antenna height can be reduced from 12.1 mm to 7.5 mm and the low frequency cutoff (│S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>│ < -10 dB) can be improved from 1.38 GHz to 730 MHz without additional volume. These improvements allow for better implementation of the HCLA in diverse telemetry, imaging, and sensing applications.

articleTitle: UWB Anisotropic Cross Polarization Conversion Metasurface with Low Sensitivity to Incident Angle
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A novel compact ultra-wideband (UWB) metasurface is designed and simulated for cross polarization conversion (CPC) with minimal changes observed across different incident angles. The proposed anisotropic metasurface achieves an excellent polarization conversion ratio (PCR) exceeding 90% across the ultra-wideband spectrum. The metasufrace consists of coupled split-ring-resonators (SRRs) and a metallic ground plane, and it is built on RT/Duroid 5880 to supports high frequency. It demonstrates an efficient cross polarization conversion ranging from 13.5 GHz to 32.7 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 83% at 3 dB. Furthermore, the PCR above 90% operates within a bandwidth from 14.6 GHz to 29.4 GHz, with a fractional bandwidth of 67%. The proposed design maintains a PCR above 80% for most of the frequency range, even as the incident wave angle varies up to 45°. The metasurface unit size is 3.3 × 3.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,

articleTitle: A Dual-State Active Wideband Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In our recent work, we introduced a cost-effective technique for designing wide-band reconfigurable reflectarray antennas (RAs). Building on this, we now present a simple yet elegant biasing network that reconfigures such RAs. This novel diode- enabled biasing network is designed to minimize RF interference while optimizing DC performance. Notably, a 10 × 10 element array is developed, demonstrating stable beam reconfigurability across the entire 8.85 GHz to 11.75 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Dipole Antenna Integrated with Wideband Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a low-profile dipole antenna integrated with a wideband polarization converter metasurface. The antenna consists of a modified dipole structure that includes two parasitic patches placed on the bottom side of a single-layer, ultra-thin substrate in a coplanar configuration. A 2 × 2 metasurface array is positioned on the top side of the substrate to convert linear polarization to circular polarization. Each unit cell of the metasurface consists of a complementary patch structure formed by etching out two diagonally oriented striplines from the metal square patch, resulting in a distinct chiseled pattern. These diagonal striplines are essential for creating 90° phase difference and achieving near-equal amplitude between orthogonal polarization components. The proposed antenna achieves a wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 42.1% (4.06-6.22 GHz) and an impedance bandwidth of 44.2% (4.06-6.36 GHz), with a peak gain of 3.2 dBi at 5.2 GHz and a radiation efficiency of over 95% within the AR bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design of an Efficient System for Infrared Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: The paper presents a system for infrared energy harvesting. The system consists of two antennas. One antenna works at the near-infrared (1um wavelength) and accepts power from solar radiation. The estimated accepted power is higher than that can be received by conventional solar cells. The other antenna accepts power radiated from the earth's surface at a wavelength of 10 um. The estimated received power reaches 250 watts per square meter when the antenna gains 3 dB.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Pattern-to-Code Mapping for Digital Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a method for mapping pattern masks to coding sequences using a convolutional neural network (CNN). To assess the feasibility of this approach, we generated a dataset based on a numerically simulated 15 × 15, 2-bit spatially coded digital metasurface operating at 100 GHz. The CNN model was trained to predict the coding sequence required to produce a specific pattern mask. The mask was generated by assigning a value of ‘1’ if the radiation exceeded one-tenth of the maximum value, and ‘0’ otherwise. The model performance was evaluated by the error, defined as the difference in magnitude between the actual and predicted patterns.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Phased Lens Array Antenna With Anti-Reflection Structure Fed by Circular-Arc Arranged Horns in 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Dielectric lens antennas, known for their high gain and low feed loss, are promising candidates for use in the 300 GHz band. One of the serious problems associated with lens antennas is their considerable height. This paper presents the design of a phased lens-array antenna, where the primary radiators are horn antennas arranged in a circular arc. By adjusting the phase difference between elements, the antenna can scan each multiple beam. Furthermore, employing a high dielectric constant material for the lens and introducing an anti-reflection structure on the surface reduces the antenna's height. Electromagnetic simulations demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves a gain of over 30 dBi within an angular range of ±20°, while maintaining high efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced mmWave Slot-Ring Phased Array Antenna with Polarization Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Polarization reconfiguration in phased array antennas is gaining attention due to its ability to reduce multipath fading, which is crucial in mmWave frequency bands. This paper presents a 2×2 slot-ring phased array antenna designed for mmWave 5G NR (n257 and n258) bands. At these higher frequencies, the small size of the radiation aperture and the narrow spacing between antenna elements present design challenges. To address this, a novel feeding technique is proposed for the antenna array. The antenna comprises six layers-three metal and three dielectric layers. The top-layer microstrip line is connected via a metalized hole with a diameter of 0.2 mm, while the antenna aperture is connected through several ground vias with a diameter of 0.15 mm. This feeding technique provides flexibility for integrating surface-mounted phase shifters, enabling the generation of appropriate phase shifts at each array port, which are necessary for polarization state changes. The antenna operates from 24.5 to 29.5 GHz, achieving a 20% fractional bandwidth and 8.5 dBi gain. Additionally, the array is capable of beam steering within a ±20-degree range without creating any grating lobes.

articleTitle: An Ultrathin Terahertz Tri-Band Fractal Meta-Absorber for Liquid Chemical Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: An ultrathin, single-layer planar terahertz meta-material absorber (MMA) is numerically demonstrated for sensing applications. The tri-band fractal MMA consists of a Cayley tree-shaped resonator deposited on a polyimide substrate. The designed absorber is polarization-insensitive and has three resonance frequencies at 3.997, 6.98, and 8.795 THz. For the absorption peak at 3.997 THz, the proposed sensor has thickness of 0.08 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and its largest dimension is 0.45 A. The electric field map is analysed to interpret the fundamental characteristics of the three resonances. The refractive index based sensing is evaluated by placing a container on top of the resonating surface that holds the analyte. The proposed sensor exhibits a good Quality factor (Q) value of 97.7 and its highest sensitivity is 0.44 THz/RIU. The designed MMA sensor is suitable for various chemical and bio sensing purposes.

articleTitle: Compact Ultrawideband Slotted Bowtie-Dipole Antenna with 136.5% FBW for Next-Generation Wireless Communication and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This study introduces a compact ultrawideband bowtie antenna architecture with a tapered slot feed for wireless communication and sensing applications. The design features a modified bowtie-dipole antenna configuration with incorporated circular slots for bandwidth enhancement and a tapered slot feed for improved impedance matching. The substrate used is FR-4, with a dielectric constant of 4.3 and a tangent loss of 0.025. A 1 Oz (0.035 mm) copper patch is employed. A peak gain of 7.24 dBi is achieved at a center frequency of 9.24 GHz. The overall dimensions of the proposed design are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.63\lambda\times 1.73\lambda$</tex>. The antenna achieves a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 136.5%, operating within a frequency range from 2.93 GHz to 15.55 GHz. It is designed for easy integration with most printed circuit board (PCB) designs, making it well-suited for broadband wireless communication and sensing applications.

articleTitle: Ridge Gap Waveguide Slotted Array Antenna for Millimeter Wave Application - Comparative Use Case Scenario
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Three scenarios of slotted array antenna based on ridge gap waveguide technology (RGW) for mmWave applications are investigated. These cases include different slot arrays: transverse, split transverse, and longitudinal slots within a frequency range of 60 to 70 GHz. The structure of the antennas and the number of slots is identical, with open terminations, while the dimensions of the slots vary. A comparative analysis of bandwidth, peak realized gain, and efficiency is reported. The transverse slotted array antenna offers higher bandwidth and greater efficiency compared to the other two proposed antennas.

articleTitle: Communication Between Rectangular Phased Arrays on an Orbital-Angular-Momentum-Encoded Link
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: We demonstrate a point-to-point orbital angular momentum (OAM) free-space radio frequency link at 26.5 GHz in an indoor far-field anechoic chamber. OAM modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell=\pm 1$</tex> are generated by a rectangular phased array antenna and transmitted to a similar array for detection. This is done in contrast to much of the existing work on utilizing OAM to increase communication link capacity, which have tended to focus on the use of purpose-built uniform circular arrays [1]–[5]. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Es/No$</tex> is measured for several configurations of the transmitter and receiver pair to estimate modal crosstalk and baseline performance, and a study on how link performance is impacted by phase precision is described. We find that readily available rectangular phased array antennas can exhibit sufficient performance - suppression in excess of 20 dB for undesired modes - to warrant consideration for nearer-term implementation of OAM multiplexing into the telecommunications infrastructure.

articleTitle: Prior Knowledge-Guided Deep Learning-Enabled Metantenna Optimization and Synthesis (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper reviews recent advances in deep learning (DL)-enabled techniques for optimizing and synthesizing metamaterial-based antennas (metantennas). Expanding the degrees of freedom (DoF) of design of metamaterials and metasurfaces creates new opportunities for innovative metantenna designs by the introduction of novel physical properties. However, the increased DoF also increases significant complexity of the design process. To tackle this challenge, prior-knowledge-guided deep learning-enabled (PK-DL) optimization and synthesis methods have been proposed and developed. These methods integrate prior knowledge into deep learning algorithms, such as artificial neural networks (ANNs) and conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (cDCGANs), to guide and accelerate metantenna design processes. Recent progress demonstrates that AI algorithms applied to antenna design open new opportunities for optimizing and synthesizing metantennas with enhanced performance and multifunctional capabilities.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Low-SAR Antennas for Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this article, a metal framed mobile phone antenna with high efficiency and low SAR value has been proposed for use in the sub-6G frequency band. The proposed antenna is based on IFA and uses multiple feeding points and floor slits to make the current distribution more uniform, resulting in multiple hotspots in SAR distribution, achieving high antenna efficiency and reducing SAR values on multiple surfaces. The measured results show that the -6db bandwidth of the proposed antenna can cover 3.38-3.74GHz, and can cover the Sub-6G frequency band. The efficiency is above 50% in the Sub-6G frequency band, and the maximum SAR value can be reduced by more than 30%.

articleTitle: Rectangular Waveguide Flange Aperture-Shared Antenna with Extended Array Angle-of-Arrival
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In the decommissioning work of the Fukushima Nuclear Power Plant, an aperture-shared antenna with an extended array angle-of-arrival estimation to estimate the location of sensors inside a primary containment vessel is proposed. The proposed antenna comprises a downlink antenna consisting of an open-ended rectangular waveguide and an uplink microstrip array antenna with eight elements configured on a waveguide flange. By performing array expansion processing on the array antenna on the flange, it is possible to suppress the grating lobes caused by the sparse array arrangement and wide-angle direction-of-arrival estimation can be realized.

articleTitle: An FPT-Based mmW Cavity-Backed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this work, a cavity-backed antenna with increased bandwidth and minimum design complexity for operation at millimeter wave (mmW) frequencies is proposed. Namely, by leveraging our recently proposed frequency pulling technique (FPT) and aperture coupled feeding mechanisms we increase the bandwidth of our antenna 1.8 times compared to conventional cavity-backed designs found in the literature without compromising directivity, radiation efficiency and size. This design is a good candidate for practical applications in next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Effects of Dust, Sweat, and Moisture on a Dual-Band Wearable WiFi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Wearable antennas can be integrated with WiFi wearable systems. The author has previously proposed a dualband textile antenna for WiFi applications [1] working at 2.45 GHz and 5.5 GHz bands. This study investigates the impact of everyday wear and tear, including dust, moisture, and sweat, on the performance of a proposed textile dual-band WiFi antenna. Results indicate that the presence of a conductive insulating layer prevents sweat and moisture from significantly affecting performance when in contact with the skin. While dust on the surface of the radiating element does not substantially impact the antenna's functionality, dust accumulating on the feedline can cause a frequency shift and reduce the antenna's gain.

articleTitle: Towards Bi-Directional Deep Learning Approach in Patch Antenna Design and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the design and optimization of high-gain bidirectional antennas using deep learning, aimed at reducing the computational complexity and energy consumption associated with traditional iterative simulation methods. By leveraging a neural network model trained on six key antenna parameters, our approach enables bidirectional functionality. It predicts the S11 parameter and gain from given antenna geometrical parameters, and inversely, determines the optimal antenna geometrical parameters based on desired S11 and gain values within the frequency band of 3.25 to 4.25 GHz. This dual capability not only accelerates the design process but also minimizes the need for extensive simulations, thereby conserving computational resources. The results significantly reducing the energy and time required for antenna design and optimization. The antenna is designed on a Rogers 5880 substrate with a thickness of 62 mils, and both simulation and measured results validate the high performance and efficiency of the proposed bidirectional antenna

articleTitle: A Low-Profile, Closely-Spaced 1 ×4 MIMO Array with Low Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: A single-layered, 1×4 linear array antenna, consisting of closely-spaced microstrip patches, is presented and investigated in this paper. The mutual coupling is reduced by utilizing a decoupling structure integrated within the array to generate a 180-degree phase reversal with the interfering signal. Compared to conventional probe-fed coupled arrays, the proposed antenna design realized a significant improvement in isolation levels between the elements, increasing from ∼4 dB to over 19 dB. More importantly, the proposed linear array is compact with a center-to-center element spacing of ∼0.26λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and an edge-to-edge spacing of only about 0.016λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Design of Lightweight Perforated Pyramidal Horn Antenna with Constant Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This study addresses the long-standing challenge of horn antenna's bulk and weight, which limits their versatility. A novel, lightweight perforated pyramidal horn antenna is proposed, achieving a constant beamwidth and operating in the X-band (8–12 GHz) with a resonance frequency of 10 GHz, VSWR < 2, and return loss < −10 dB. These results were simulated in the Antenna Toolbox from MATLAB. This design reduces weight by 30% compared to traditional designs, enabled by advanced computational optimization techniques. Simulations demonstrate outstanding performance in radiation pattern, gain, beamwidth, return loss, VSWR, and polarization. The antenna's consistent beamwidth and superior radiation characteristics make it an ideal solution for satellite communications, radar systems, RF jammers on naval platforms, and airborne and shipborne applications where high performance and reduced weight are essential.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Reflective Electromagnetic Surfaces with Switching Capability for K-Band Polarizer Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Reflective Electromagnetic Surfaces (RES) that function as switching polarizers in K-band frequency spectrum. The RES is designed to operate at the frequency range of 16 GHz to 25.5 GHz with the capability of switching from a regular reflector to a polarizer that converts linearly polarized incoming waves into circularly polarized reflected waves. Observations of the co-polarization and cross-polarization reflection coefficients, axial ratio, and surface current distribution on the simulated RES confirm both regular non-polarizer reflector and polarizer functionality. Validation is performed by measuring realized RES samples, consisting of 30×30 unit cells, in both on-state and off-state conditions. The measurement results show co-polarization and cross-polarization magnitudes similar to the simulations. The magnitude of measured cross-polarization reflection coefficient is 5 dB lower than the simulation, indicating the need of better material usage in RES realization for loss reduction.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Transparent Antenna for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: In this paper, a compact transparent antenna featuring a new TE-shaped indium tin oxide (ITO) radiating patch, an ITO ground plane, and a plexiglass substrate has been designed for 5G transparent communication. A transparent conductor, utilizing a thin film of ITO instead of a traditional copper sheet, is selected for its superior performance as a transparent antenna. The new antenna, composed of a TE-shaped ITO radiating patch and an ITO ground plane with a plexiglass substrate, achieves wideband performance. The antenna's overall dimensions are 1.48 × 1.35 × 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, maintaining 85% transparency. The antenna operates over a reflection coefficient range of 65.3 GHz to 68.7 GHz at S11<-10 dB (bandwidth). A gain above 5.5 dBi at the entire operating frequency with a stable radiation pattern is observed. The proposed antenna demonstrates good radiation characteristics, making it well-suited for various applications in vehicular communication and other scenarios.

articleTitle: Multilayer, Multiband Compact Wearable Endfire Antenna for On-Body Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: This paper investigates a compact, multilayered, multiband end-fire Yagi-Uda antenna through simulation in free space and on phantom. The antenna's design utilizes alternating layers of denim and latex substrates to achieve the desired end-fire radiation pattern. The proposed structure with phantom demonstrates three distinct end-fire radiations at resonant frequencies of 4.82 GHz, 5.22 GHz, and 5.65 GHz, with beam directions at angles of 22°, 40°, and 9°, and corresponding main beam directivities of 8.56 dBi, 9.25 dBi, and 3.60 dBi, respectively. To enhance beam performance near the human body and ensure compliance with Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) requirements, a 0.1 mm thick aluminum layer is added to the antenna's rear side. SAR analyses for 1 g and 10 g of tissue yielded values of 1.42 W/kg and 0.54 W/kg, respectively, meeting international safety standards.

articleTitle: Enabling Non-Contact Heart Rate Monitoring with Readily Available mmW Radars
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Non-contact vital sign detection has emerged as an innovative solution in healthcare, offering the potential for continuous, non-invasive monitoring. This paper focuses on non-contact heart rate (HR) detection, a critical physiological parameter for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular health. The reliable and accurate acquisition of HR responses has been made possible at a commercial level through various approaches. However, as shown in this paper, fully accurate non-contact heart rate acquisition is yet to be achieved.

articleTitle: Advanced Nested Array Configuration Achieving Large-Scale Hole-Free Co-Array in MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Antenna Technology (iWAT)
abstract: Generally, a large number of antennas are used in the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system for various desirable merits. This paper introduces the advanced nested antenna array (ANAA), a sparse array structure, into the MIMO system to increase the spatial resolution and provide more degrees of freedom (DOFs). The ANAA effectively configures two uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and places two antennas between them. As such, the ANAA produces a hole-free difference co-array. Compared with the existing designs, the ANAA benefits from simple closed-form expressions for its construction and optimized distribution of the total number of antennas. Meanwhile, it provides more DOFs with a wider hole-free co-array aperture. The theoretical propositions are proved, and performance results confirm the superiority of the proposed ANAA configuration.
